claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a theory-grounded plug-in correction, MASA can be added to existing sparse attention frameworks without changing their sparse kernels or budgets.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into existing sparse attention frameworks without modifying kernels or budgets

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Extensive experiments across multiple sparse attention methods, benchmarks, and LLM backbones show consistent accuracy gains, supporting both MASA and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: Experiments across multiple methods, benchmarks, and backbones show consistent accuracy gains with MASA

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As a result, MASA can be added to diverse sparse attention frameworks without changing their implementation interface.
claims.claim_summary: MASA fits diverse sparse attention frameworks without modifying implementation interfaces

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA can be integrated into existing sparse attention baselines while keeping their sparse kernels and budgets unchanged.
claims.claim_summary: MASA integrates into existing baselines preserving their kernels and budgets

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under matched settings with the original baselines, MASA gives consistent accuracy gains, supporting both the proposed method and the matrix-approximation view of sparse attention.
claims.claim_summary: Matched evaluations confirm consistent accuracy improvements across baselines using MASA

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA therefore does not require a new full-resolution dense attention map beyond the information used for sparse-unit ranking.
claims.claim_summary: MASA requires no additional full-resolution dense attention map beyond standard profile ranking

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This computation only uses matrix products and score matrices at the profile resolution, without materializing the N × N × r contribution tensor.
claims.claim_summary: MASA score computation is memory-safe and avoids materializing full three-dimensional contribution tensors

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MASA improves all eight matched average scores across three sparse methods, three benchmark suites, and both Llama- and Qwen-family backbones.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves all eight matched benchmark average scores across frameworks and backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On InfiniteBench, MASA raises FlexPrefill-Llama from 47.14 to 47.99 against a full-attention score of 48.06, recovering approximately 92% of the original average-score deficit.
claims.claim_summary: MASA raises FlexPrefill-Llama on InfiniteBench to 47.99, recovering 92% of accuracy deficit

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On RULER, MASA raises SeerAttention from 87.60 to 88.09, moving it from below the dense reference to above it.
claims.claim_summary: MASA raises SeerAttention on RULER to 88.09, surpassing full-attention quality

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, replacing the ranking score adds 0.76 points, exceeding the original method’s 0.48-point advantage over full attention and increasing that advantage to 1.24 points.
claims.claim_summary: MASA adds 0.76 points to FlexPrefill-Llama on RULER, expanding its margin over full attention

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the four RULER configurations at 32K, 64K, and 128K, MASA improves 11 of 12 matched length-level scores.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves 11 of 12 matched length-level RULER scores at 32K–128K context lengths

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For every configuration, the mean gain over these longer contexts at 32K–128K exceeds that at 4K–16K.
claims.claim_summary: MASA's accuracy gains are larger at longer contexts (32K–128K) than shorter ones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 128K, MASA improves MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen by 1.28, 0.48, 1.45, and 2.16 points, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: At 128K sequence length, MASA improves accuracy across all four evaluated models and methods

claims.claim_text_verbatim: At 64K, the gains reach 2.16 points for FlexPrefill-Llama and 3.65 points for FlexPrefill-Qwen.
claims.claim_summary: At 64K length, MASA increases FlexPrefill scores by up to 3.65 points

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On LongBench, MASA improves SeerAttention’s 8K+ score from 52.69 to 53.16.
claims.claim_summary: MASA improves SeerAttention's long-context 8K+ LongBench score from 52.69 to 53.16

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The evaluated MASA configurations reduce normalized squared output error in all four framework–backbone pairs, providing direct empirical support for matrix-product preservation.
claims.claim_summary: MASA reduces normalized attention output approximation error across all evaluated frameworks and backbones

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across MInference, SeerAttention, FlexPrefill-Llama, and FlexPrefill-Qwen, replacing the original ranking score with MASA adds empirically negligible overhead relative to the sparse attention runtime and remains far below the dense attention cost.
claims.claim_summary: MASA introduces negligible runtime overhead over baseline sparse attention mechanisms

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Therefore, MASA improves accuracy without weakening the practical efficiency of the underlying sparse attention method.
claims.claim_summary: MASA increases accuracy without reducing the practical efficiency of sparse attention baselines

claims.claim_text_verbatim: First, raw MASA already improves the original sparse baseline in several settings, which supports the matrix-product scoring objective itself.
claims.claim_summary: Raw MASA score improves baseline accuracy, validating the matrix-product preservation metric

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Second, norm control can further improve the score in settings where value-norm outliers affect sparse-unit ranking.
claims.claim_summary: Norm control methods mitigate outlier value norms and improve sparse ranking results

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Norm clipping is helpful for SeerAttention and FlexPrefill-Llama, while soft norm balancing is useful in some FlexPrefill settings.
claims.claim_summary: Norm clipping benefits SeerAttention and FlexPrefill-Llama while soft norm balancing aids FlexPrefill

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 8: Attention-output error decreases across all four evaluated framework–backbone pairs.
claims.claim_summary: Attention-output error decreases across all four evaluated framework–backbone pairs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The relative reductions are 0.41% for MInference, 2.10% for SeerAttention, and 2.34% and 7.17% for FlexPrefill on Llama and Qwen, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: MASA achieves up to 7.17% relative reduction in normalized attention-output error

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The evaluated MASA configurations produce outputs closer to dense attention, providing empirical support for the matrix-approximation view alongside the downstream accuracy results.
claims.claim_summary: MASA output vectors closely match dense attention outputs, validating the matrix approximation hypothesis
